mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which leads to higher borrowing costs and reduced corporate investments, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS increased by more than 0.5% in the last month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within the last month indicates weakening labor market conditions, which leads to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE increased by more than 0.5% in the last month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over the last three months signals strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate revenues and earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances where RSAFS increased over the last three months.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% over the last two months signals supply-side constraints, which can lead to reduced corporate output and earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO declined by more than 2% in the last two months.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is above 6% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) decline for two consecutive months, it indicates a weakening labor market, which leads to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 6% and PAYEMS declines for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances where UNRATE > 6% and PAYEMS declined for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) increase by more than 5% over the last two months and real GDP (GDPC1) grows by more than 2% year-over-year, it signals strong economic demand, which boosts corporate revenues and earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases > 5% in 2 months and GDPC1 grows > 2% YoY
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances where HOUST increased by more than 5% and GDPC1 grew by more than 2% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.25% within the last month signals an accommodative monetary policy, which leads to lower borrowing costs and increased investments, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS decreased by more than 0.25% in the last month.

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 2% year-over-year and industrial production (INDPRO) declines by more than 1% in the last month, it signals inflationary pressures and supply constraints, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases > 2% YoY and INDPRO declines > 1% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances where CPIAUCSL increased by more than 2% YoY and INDPRO declined by more than 1% in the last month.
